questions.text: Burking is:
questions.explanation: Burking combines compression of the chest (traumatic asphyxia) with closure of the nose and mouth (smothering). This is the Burke and Hare method.
questions.eshrahly:
Burking is a homicidal method that joins two mechanisms. The killer kneels or sits on the victim's chest while closing the nose and mouth with a hand (Burke and Hare, Edinburgh 1828). It may leave few external signs. Smothering by itself rarely produces petechiae, significant cyanosis or congestion unless the victim struggles. Traumatic asphyxia, in contrast, produces dramatic congestion and petechiae.
MechanismWhat happensTypical manner
Traumatic asphyxiaA heavy weight presses on the chest or upper abdomen and makes respiration impossible. Findings: congestion, cyanosis, petechiae, a line of demarcation.Mostly accidental, may be homicidal
SmotheringThe external respiratory openings are occluded by a hand or soft objects.Homicidal or accidental
BurkingTraumatic asphyxia and smothering together.Homicidal

questions.text: The most common cause of inward (central) hyoid bone fracture is:
questions.explanation: Throttling (manual strangulation) is the most common cause of hyoid bone fracture, and the fracture is inward.
questions.eshrahly:
Throttling is constriction of the neck by the hand. The direct, forceful and repeated finger pressure damages the deep neck structures. Its findings are multiple contusions and fingernail abrasions on the neck, inward fracture of the hyoid and of the thyroid cartilage, and contusions of the deep tissues of the neck. Throttling is homicidal by definition, because grip relaxes as consciousness is lost.
Form of neck compressionInternal neck findings
ThrottlingInward hyoid fracture (the most common cause of hyoid fracture), thyroid cartilage fracture, deep muscle bruising
Ligature strangulationInward hyoid fracture, possible thyroid cartilage fracture, contusions and lacerations of neck muscles
Ordinary (suicidal) hangingUsually little internal damage
Judicial long-drop hangingExtensive neck laceration, torn sternomastoids, fracture-dislocation of C2–C3

questions.text: Which method of asphyxia shows MOST severe internal neck damage:
questions.explanation: Throttling involves direct, forceful, repeated finger pressure, which causes extensive deep-muscle bruising and fractures of the hyoid and thyroid cartilage. Ordinary hanging usually causes little internal damage.
questions.eshrahly:
The amount of internal damage follows how the force is applied. In throttling the hand grips the neck directly. This explains the deep contusions and the cartilage and hyoid fractures. In ordinary hanging the body's own weight acts through a ligature, and internal damage is usually minimal. Massive damage in a hanging suggests a judicial long drop. The cause of death also differs between the forms.

Throttling causes death by:
- mechanical anoxia
- reflex cardiac inhibition
- cerebral anoxia
- delayed glottic oedema and choking

Hanging causes death mainly by cerebral ischaemia from carotid compression, with vagal cardiac inhibition and mechanical anoxia also contributing. Severe internal neck injury should therefore point first to throttling, or to a judicial hanging.

questions.text: Which one causes severe damage to internal neck structures:
questions.explanation: Throttling produces extensive deep-muscle bruising and fractures of the hyoid and thyroid cartilage. Ordinary hanging, complete or incomplete, usually causes little internal damage.
questions.eshrahly:
Complete and incomplete hanging are both suspension of the body from the neck by a ligature. They differ in how much of the body weight is carried by the ligature, not in the amount of internal injury.
FeatureComplete hangingIncomplete hanging
Body weightFully suspended, feet off the groundPartly suspended, feet or knees may touch the ground
Main cause of deathCerebral ischaemiaAsphyxia
FaceLess congested, sometimes paleMarkedly congested
Internal neck damageUsually little in ordinary hanging. Massive damage means judicial long-drop hanging.
Throttling is the form in which deep neck tissues and cartilages are directly crushed by fingers.

questions.text: The findings on the neck: extensive laceration, tears in sternomastoid and fracture-dislocation of C2-C3 vertebrae. These findings are present in:
questions.explanation: Extensive neck lacerations, torn sternomastoids and C2–C3 fracture-dislocation (hangman's fracture) with cord transection are the picture of judicial (long-drop) hanging. Ordinary hanging usually causes little internal damage.
questions.eshrahly:
Judicial (long-drop) hanging is the form in which the cause of death is transection of the spinal cord, and death is instant. The characteristic findings are extensive neck lacerations, torn sternomastoid muscles, and fracture-dislocation of C2–C3, the "hangman's fracture" of C2 (a bilateral pars-articularis fracture). This differs from the other forms of hanging. In suicidal, accidental, incomplete and autoerotic hanging, the neck usually shows only a ligature mark, and death is mainly from cerebral ischaemia, vagal inhibition or mechanical anoxia.

Autoerotic (sexual) asphyxia is usually by hanging, with anoxia induced deliberately to heighten arousal. It can resemble a suicidal hanging, but it does not produce this destructive neck injury.

questions.text: Ligature mark of strangulation characteristics:
questions.explanation: A ligature strangulation mark is transverse (horizontal), low (below the thyroid cartilage) and complete (encircles the whole neck). Hanging is the opposite: oblique, high and incomplete.
questions.eshrahly:
In strangulation, the constricting force comes from the ligature itself, and it is applied evenly around the neck. In hanging, the body weight pulls the ligature upward toward the suspension point.
Feature of the ligature markHanging (incomplete)Ligature strangulation
LevelHigh, above the thyroid cartilageLow, below the thyroid cartilage
DirectionObliqueTransverse
ContinuityIncomplete (does not encircle the neck)Complete (encircles the neck)
DepthDeep, fading gradually toward the suspension pointDeep all through
The mark may show the shape of the ligating material, as a crush abrasion with a parchment-like quality. It is less visible with thick hair, a high collar, or a broad, soft ligature. It is more visible with a thin, rough, wire or metal ligature and with a longer duration of constriction.

questions.text: Strangulation with ligature:
options: Associated with multiple lines on the neck
Marks are high in the neck
originalOptions: Associated with multiple lines on the neck
Marks are high in the neck
questions.explanation: Ligature strangulation produces transverse, complete marks low in the neck. This is the reverse of hanging, whose marks are high, oblique and incomplete.
questions.eshrahly:
Ligature strangulation is mechanical anoxic death caused by constriction of the neck by a ligature that occludes the air passages from outside. The constricting force is not the body's own suspended weight, which is the difference from hanging.

Causes of death:
- mechanical anoxia
- reflex cardiac inhibition
- delayed oedema of the glottis and choking, which can kill even some time after the ligature has been removed

Other findings:
- abrasions and contusions taking the shape of the ligating material
- inward fracture of the hyoid, possibly of the thyroid cartilage
- contusions and lacerations of neck muscles

The manner is homicidal or accidental, but not suicidal. A person cannot maintain ligature pressure on their own neck after losing consciousness. Any ligature mark on the neck is presumed to be homicide (strangulation) until proven otherwise.

questions.text: Abrasions found on the neck are always considered what until proved otherwise?
questions.explanation: Neck marks are presumed to be strangulation (homicide) until proven otherwise. This is the reverse default of hanging, which is more often self-inflicted.
questions.eshrahly:
Location matters in interpreting abrasions. An abrasion pattern on the neck raises suspicion for throttling (manual strangulation). Fingernails leave small crescent-shaped (semilunar) abrasions when pressed in, or linear scratches when dragged. These are classic on the neck in throttling. A ligature mark on the neck is a crush (pressure) abrasion that reproduces the shape of the ligating material, and it is presumed homicidal until proven otherwise.

Both throttling and ligature strangulation are, by definition or by default, homicidal. Throttling is always homicidal. Ligature strangulation is homicidal or accidental, never suicidal. Hanging, by contrast, can be suicidal, homicidal or accidental, and the manner is never assumed from the mechanism alone.

questions.text: True about the frothy secretions in drowning:
questions.explanation: Drowning froth is white (may be pink-tinged), fine, lathery, tenacious and persistent. Coarse, offensive froth is putrefactive, not drowning froth.
questions.eshrahly:
Froth at the mouth and nostrils is a sure external sign of drowning and an ante-mortem sign. It forms from air, water and mucus whipped together by continued respiratory effort. It will not form if the body was already dead and was dumped in the water afterward.
FeatureDrowning frothPutrefactive froth
ColourWhite (may be pink-tinged)Red-brown
TextureFine, latheryCoarse
PersistenceTenacious and persistent, re-forms after wipingNot described as persistent
SmellNot describedOffensive

questions.text: Froth after drowning is:
questions.explanation: Drowning froth is white (may be pink-tinged), fine and lathery, formed from air, water and mucus. Bloody or coarse froth does not describe it.
questions.eshrahly:
The signs of drowning separate into sure and probable ones.
CategorySignMeaning
Sure externalFroth at the mouth and/or nostrilsAnte-mortem sign: the victim was alive and breathing when entering the water
Sure externalCadaveric spasmAnte-mortem sign: proof of life at entry into water (e.g. clutched weeds)
ProbableCyanosisRelated to anoxic anoxia
ProbablePale, wet skin; goose skin; washerwoman's skinRelated to the body being in water
ProbablePost-mortem injuries (animal bites, water movement, sand or rocks)Occur after death in water
The key investigative question is whether the person was alive when they went into the water or already dead. Froth and cadaveric spasm answer it.

questions.text: The dead body is lying on autopsy table. There is leathery, fine, tenacious, persistent froth at mouth and nostrils. The death is due to:
questions.explanation: Fine, tenacious, persistent froth at the mouth and nostrils is the sure external sign of drowning. It is formed by respiratory effort during submersion.
questions.eshrahly:
Drowning is mechanical anoxic death due to submersion of the respiratory openings under water.

Causes of death:
- direct cause: mechanical anoxia
- indirect causes: reflex cardiac inhibition from vagal stimulation, and head injury or other fatal injuries sustained before or during submersion

The manner may be homicidal, suicidal or accidental. Water immersion alters the usual timeline of post-mortem changes, so cooling, hypostasis, adipocere and putrefaction are all affected. This matters when estimating time of death.

questions.text: In drowning, the finding most indicative of TIME PASSED since death:
questions.explanation: Washerwoman's skin shows how long the body has been in water (time since immersion), not the cause of death. Froth indicates life at entry into the water.
questions.eshrahly:
Maceration of the hands and feet begins within hours and progresses to peeling ("glove and stocking" skin) over days to weeks, faster in warm water. A body dumped after death macerates too, so it cannot show that the person drowned.
SignWhat it tells you
Froth at mouth/nostrilsAlive and breathing at submersion (ante-mortem)
Cadaveric spasmAlive at entry into the water (ante-mortem)
Washerwoman's skinDuration of immersion
Goose skin (cutis anserina)Probable sign related to the body being in water
Note that the guide words this sign as time since immersion.

questions.text: In drowning – one is indicated for time passed since death:
questions.explanation: Maceration progresses with time in water, so it indicates how long the body has been immersed. Froth is an ante-mortem sign of drowning, not a measure of time.
questions.eshrahly:
Being in water changes the normal timeline of post-mortem changes. Cooling, hypostasis, adipocere and putrefaction are all altered by immersion.

- Decomposition in water is slow, because of exclusion of air, protection by clothes and early cooling.
- Hypostasis in drowning is often faint, because moving water keeps turning the body. A floating body usually lies face-down with the head dependent, so lividity appears in the face, upper chest and upper limbs.
- Washerwoman's skin is a time-in-water marker. Goose skin is a probable sign related to the body being in water.

For these reasons, time-of-death estimates in drowning cases have to be made cautiously.

questions.text: Traumatic asphyxia shows:
questions.explanation: Chest compression blocks venous return from the head. This causes intense congestion and petechiae above the level of compression, ending at a sharp line of demarcation.
questions.eshrahly:
Traumatic asphyxia occurs when a heavy weight presses on the chest or upper abdomen and makes respiration impossible. It is typically seen in "riot-crush", when a crowd compresses the chest.
AspectDetails
Causes of deathMechanical anoxia, injury to vital organs, positional asphyxia where mechanisms overlap
FindingsContusions and abrasions of the chest and abdomen, fractured ribs, rupture of internal organs
Skin pictureIntense congestion, cyanosis and huge numbers of petechiae over face, neck and upper chest; line of demarcation between the discoloured upper body and the normal lower part
MannerMostly accidental, may be homicidal
Cherry-red colour belongs to carbon monoxide poisoning, and adipocere is a late post-mortem change.

questions.text: Clear line of demarcation on the neck is always seen in:
questions.explanation: Traumatic asphyxia produces a sharp line of demarcation at the level of chest compression, between the discoloured upper body and the normal lower part.
questions.eshrahly:
The line of demarcation is the signature of traumatic asphyxia. It marks the level of compression. Above it the face, neck and upper chest show intense congestion, cyanosis and numerous petechiae (an "ecchymotic mask"). Below it the body looks normal.

The cause is blocked venous return from the head. Hanging, gagging and drowning do not produce this pattern. Gagging means a cloth is pushed into or across the mouth, with progressive asphyxia as the nares close from mucus and oedema.

In the guide the line is at the level of compression, which is usually the chest or upper abdomen, rather than literally on the neck.

questions.text: Petechial hemorrhages are typically seen in which condition?
questions.explanation: Massive petechiae over the face, neck and upper chest point to traumatic (crush or riot) asphyxia.
questions.eshrahly:
Petechiae are pinpoint haemorrhages from rupture of small vessels, predominantly small venules. The rupture appears to be mechanical, caused by sudden over-distension after an abrupt rise in intravascular pressure. They are found above the level of the obstruction. The most common sites are the visceral pleura and the epicardium. They also appear in the conjunctivae and sclerae, where venules are unsupported by surrounding tissue.
Classical signWhat it is
CongestionRed face and head from venous filling when venous return is obstructed
OedemaTransudation of fluid from veins under raised venous pressure
CyanosisIncrease in reduced haemoglobin, observable from about 5 g/100 mL
PetechiaeRuptured venules in skin, eyes, pleura and epicardium
Petechiae are non-specific. They also occur in MI, asthma and whooping cough, so alone they do not prove asphyxia.

questions.text: Cause of death in mechanical asphyxia includes all of the following EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: Mechanical asphyxia kills by anoxia, pulmonary oedema, reflex vagal cardiac inhibition and cerebral ischaemia. Sepsis is not one of these mechanisms.
questions.eshrahly:
The underlying mechanism of death in mechanical (violent) asphyxia is usually a combination of neck compression, airway blockage, compression of the chest or face, and chemical asphyxia or lack of oxygen. Delayed glottic oedema can also kill after the ligature is removed. Reflex cardiac arrest works through a defined pathway. Pressure on the carotid sinus sends afferent impulses along the glossopharyngeal nerve (CN IX), and the efferent limb is the vagus (CN X).
TypeCauses of death
HangingCerebral ischaemia (commonest), vagal cardiac inhibition, mechanical anoxia; cord transection in judicial hanging
Ligature strangulationMechanical anoxia, reflex cardiac inhibition, delayed glottic oedema
ThrottlingMechanical anoxia, reflex cardiac inhibition, cerebral anoxia, delayed glottic oedema
ChokingReflex cardiac inhibition, mechanical anoxia
DrowningMechanical anoxia; indirect: vagal cardiac inhibition, associated head injury

questions.text: Mechanical asphyxia is type of:
questions.explanation: In mechanical (violent) asphyxia, an external force obstructing the airway prevents enough oxygen reaching the blood. This is anoxic anoxia.
questions.eshrahly:
Hypoxia means low oxygen and anoxia means without oxygen. Each type of anoxia corresponds to a failure at a different point in the oxygen chain.
TypeProblemExamples
AnoxicNot enough oxygen reaches the bloodHigh altitude, respiratory centre depression (morphine), paralysis (anaesthetics, Guillain–Barré), mechanical asphyxia, pulmonary embolism
AnaemicBlood cannot carry oxygen properlySevere anaemia, CO (carboxyhaemoglobin), haemolysis, haemorrhage
StagnantCirculation or delivery to tissue failsShock, heart failure, local vascular obstruction
HistotoxicTissues cannot use delivered oxygenCyanide (cytochrome oxidase inhibition)
Once the airway is obstructed, three stages follow: forced respiration, convulsions, and paralysis. Death occurs in about 5 minutes overall.

questions.text: The cause of death in an environment with DECREASED O2 levels will be:
questions.explanation: Low ambient oxygen (e.g. high altitude) means too little oxygen enters the blood, which is anoxic anoxia. This is the ambient subtype.
questions.eshrahly:
Anoxic anoxia has several subtypes. Mechanical is only one of them, so the option "mechanical anoxia" does not describe a low-oxygen atmosphere.
Subtype of anoxic anoxiaMechanismExample
AmbientLow ambient oxygenHigh altitude
CentralDepression of the respiratory centreMorphine overdose, medullary herniation
ParalyticPeripheral nerve injury or drug paralysisAnaesthetic drugs, Guillain–Barré
Mechanical (violent asphyxia)External force obstructing the airwaySmothering, gagging, choking, strangulation
Pulmonary blood flow obstructionNo perfusion of the lungPulmonary embolism
Normal oxygenation requires an oxygen-containing environment, a patent airway, normal lungs, blood supply to the lungs, a working respiratory centre, a normal chest wall, a functioning heart and blood able to carry oxygen.

questions.text: NOT of the TRIAD features of asphyxia:
options: Fluid in the left side of the heart
Petechial hemorrhages in skin of face and eyes
originalOptions: Fluid in the left side of the heart
Petechial hemorrhages in skin of face and eyes
questions.correctAnswer: B) Fluid in the left side of the heart
questions.correctAnswerText: Fluid in the left side of the heart
questions.explanation: The exam triad is congestion, cyanosis and petechial haemorrhages. Fluid in the left side of the heart is not a feature of asphyxia.
questions.eshrahly:
The classical features of asphyxia are found where air passages are obstructed by pressure on the neck or chest: congestion, oedema, cyanosis and petechial haemorrhages. Exam questions often use the triad of congestion, cyanosis and petechiae. Older texts describe a distended right heart and engorged great veins, not fluid in the left heart.

Points to remember:
- Increased fluidity of the blood was taught as a fifth classical feature but is now rejected, a classic exam trap.
- The signs are very non-specific and unreliable. Even several together do not prove mechanical asphyxia.
- If death occurs very rapidly, the signs may not have time to develop.
- The slower the death, the more prominent the signs.
- The correct approach combines history and circumstances, exclusion of other causes and cautious evaluation of the signs.

questions.text: How are antemortem hangings diagnosed?
options: By the presence of cadaveric spasm
By vital reaction signs (hemorrhage in ligature mark, skin abrasion)
originalOptions: By the presence of cadaveric spasm
By vital reaction signs (hemorrhage in ligature mark, skin abrasion)
questions.correctAnswer: B) By vital reaction signs (hemorrhage in ligature mark, skin abrasion)
questions.correctAnswerText: By vital reaction signs (hemorrhage in ligature mark, skin abrasion)
questions.explanation: Ante-mortem hanging is proved by vital reaction in the ligature mark: bruising or haemorrhage in the base and margins of the groove, reddened edges, and inflammatory cells on histology.
questions.eshrahly:
A body hanged after death shows a pale, parchment-like groove with no vital reaction. In ante-mortem hanging the ligature mark shows bruising and haemorrhage in the base and margins, with reddened edges and inflammatory cells on histology. Supporting findings are dribbling of saliva, congestion and petechiae above the mark, and carotid intimal tears.

Caution on timing: white blood cells remain capable of movement for up to 12 hours after cardiac arrest. This makes microscopic identification of a vital reaction of doubtful reliability when judging ante- versus post-mortem timing.

Cadaveric spasm and livor patterns are not the diagnostic test for ante-mortem hanging.

questions.text: Sign of antemortem hanging:
questions.explanation: Dribbling of saliva is the most important sign for hanging and is an ante-mortem sign.
questions.eshrahly:
The post-mortem picture of hanging has general and special features.
FeatureFinding in hanging
TongueProtrusion
SalivaDribbling: the most important sign, ante-mortem
HypostasisLower half of the body
NeckElongated, with the head tilted to the opposite side from the suspension point
Ligature markHigh, oblique and incomplete, with an imprint of the ligature material
Asphyxial signs are non-specific: congestion alone or petechiae alone do not prove hanging.

questions.text: Dripping of saliva occurs in:
questions.explanation: Dribbling of saliva is an ante-mortem sign of hanging, so it is not seen in a body hanged after death.
questions.eshrahly:
Saliva dribbling is the most important sign for hanging. It is an ante-mortem finding, which makes it useful in separating a true hanging from a body strung up after death. It differs between the two forms of hanging.
PointComplete hangingIncomplete hanging
Dribbling of salivaPositiveNegative
Tear in carotid intimaPositiveNegative
FaceLess congested, sometimes paleMarkedly congested
Manner may be suicidal, homicidal or accidental.

questions.text: Hypostasis in lower limbs is a sign of:
questions.explanation: In complete hanging the body is fully suspended, so blood pools in the dependent lower half. In incomplete hanging the hypostasis follows whichever part touches the ground.
questions.eshrahly:
After death, blood moves only under gravity, so lividity shows the posture of the body. Lividity starts immediately, is apparent after about 2 hours, and begins to fix around 6–8 hours. Before fixation it can shift if the body is moved. A body moved after death may show two overlapping patterns (dual lividity).
Body positionDistribution of lividity
Vertical (hanging)Distal: legs, feet, hands
Incomplete hangingAccording to the part touching the ground
Drowning (floating face-down)Chest, upper chest, upper limbs

questions.text: Abrasions around the mouth indicate:
questions.explanation: Smothering involves a hand or soft object over the nose and mouth. Fingernail abrasions around the nose and mouth are classic.
questions.eshrahly:
Smothering is mechanical anoxic death caused by occlusion of the external respiratory openings by the hand or soft objects. Findings are multiple contusions and fingernail abrasions, contusions in the buccal mucosa, and ventral hypostasis in cot death. If the victim struggles, there may be bruises and abrasions on the face and lips and inside the mouth, where the lips are pressed against the teeth.

Smothering may leave almost no signs.
- Pressure over the nose and mouth only very rarely causes petechiae, significant cyanosis or congestion unless the victim struggles.
- It may be virtually impossible to diagnose in the old, the infirm or the very young. This matters for elder abuse and infant deaths that may be mistaken for natural or SIDS deaths.
- Plastic bag suffocation typically shows no classic asphyxial signs, and the face is usually pale. The "Exit" method is an example.

Manner is homicidal or accidental.

questions.text: Manner of death in choking:
questions.explanation: Choking is mainly accidental, classically a small child choking on a button or small object. Homicidal choking is possible in principle but rare.
questions.eshrahly:
Choking is mechanical anoxic death from occlusion of the respiratory passages from inside, at the larynx, classically by a foreign body. It can cause sudden cardiac death through vagal reflex pathways, not only by blocking airflow. Causes of death are reflex cardiac inhibition and mechanical anoxia.
TypeSite/mechanism of obstructionManner
SmotheringExternal openings (nose, mouth) occluded by hand or soft objectHomicidal or accidental
GaggingCloth pushed into or across the mouth; breathing continues via the nose at firstOften seen in robbery
ChokingRespiratory passages occluded from inside, at the larynxMainly accidental

questions.text: Histotoxic anoxia is caused by:
questions.explanation: Cyanide inhibits cytochrome oxidase, so tissues cannot use oxygen even though delivery is normal. This is histotoxic anoxia.
questions.eshrahly:
In histotoxic anoxia, oxygen is delivered normally but the cells cannot use it. The classic cause is cyanide, which inhibits cytochrome oxidase. The same mitochondrial enzyme is affected by carbon monoxide, discussed in the toxicology section.

How the other options relate:
- CO is classed as anaemic anoxia in the guide: it forms carboxyhaemoglobin, which reduces the blood's ability to carry oxygen.
- Morphine causes anoxic anoxia of the central type, by depressing the respiratory centre.

Lividity colour is cherry pink in CO poisoning, in cold, and in cyanide poisoning.

questions.text: Complete hanging is related to:
questions.explanation: Complete hanging means the full body weight is suspended with the feet off the ground. Incomplete hanging is partial suspension.
questions.eshrahly:
A common misconception is that hanging requires the full body weight to be suspended in the air. Incomplete hanging, with feet or knees still touching the ground, can still be fatal. A hanging survivor should be kept under observation even if apparently well, because laryngeal oedema from neck compression may compromise the airway later.
PointComplete hangingIncomplete hanging
Other nameHigh point hangingLow point hanging
Touching the groundNegativePositive
Main cause of deathCerebral ischaemiaAsphyxia
HypostasisLower half of the bodyAccording to the part touching the ground
KnotFixed knot or running nooseAlways a running noose
Ligature markIncomplete, above the thyroid cartilage, oblique, deep, fading toward the suspension pointComplete, below the thyroid cartilage, transverse, deep all through

questions.text: Death of 65-year-old person dropped in sea water. Skin showing goose skin appearance, hair easily removed. Right hand grasping forcefully grass weeds. This is consistent with:
questions.explanation: Forceful grasping of weeds or grass in a drowning victim is cadaveric spasm. It proves the person was alive at the time of entry into the water.
questions.eshrahly:
Cadaveric spasm (instantaneous rigor) occurs at the moment of death and may persist into the period of rigor mortis. Its cause is unknown, but it is usually associated with violent deaths with intense emotion. It affects only selected muscles that were contracted at death, and it often demonstrates the last activity before death, for example gripping a knife.
PointRigor mortisCadaveric spasm
OnsetDelayed, 2–3 hoursInstantaneous
DurationUp to 36 hoursA few hours, until replaced by rigor
IntensityComparatively moderateComparatively very strong
MechanismATP falls below a critical levelUnknown
MusclesAll muscles, graduallyOnly muscles contracted at death
Goose skin is a probable drowning sign. Cadaveric spasm is one of the sure ante-mortem drowning signs.

questions.text: Guillain-Barré syndrome (GBS) causes what type of anoxia:
options: Anoxic anoxia (hypoxic hypoxia) – respiratory muscle paralysis prevents air entry
originalOptions: Anoxic anoxia (hypoxic hypoxia) – respiratory muscle paralysis prevents air entry
questions.correctAnswer: A) Anoxic anoxia (hypoxic hypoxia) – respiratory muscle paralysis prevents air entry
questions.correctAnswerText: Anoxic anoxia (hypoxic hypoxia) – respiratory muscle paralysis prevents air entry
questions.explanation: Guillain–Barré causes paralytic anoxic anoxia. Peripheral nerve injury stops respiration, so not enough oxygen reaches the blood.
questions.eshrahly:
Anoxic anoxia means oxygen does not reach the blood in adequate amounts. The paralytic subtype covers anaesthetic drugs and Guillain–Barré syndrome with peripheral nerve injury. It should be distinguished from the central subtype (respiratory centre depression, e.g. morphine overdose or medullary herniation).
Site of failureExample
Respiratory centreMorphine overdose, medullary herniation
Peripheral nerves / musclesGuillain–Barré, anaesthetic drugs
AirwayMechanical asphyxia
Pulmonary blood flowPulmonary embolism

questions.text: What type of asphyxia is caused by cyanide (HCN)?
questions.explanation: Cyanide inhibits cytochrome oxidase. Oxygen is delivered normally, but the tissues cannot retrieve it.
questions.eshrahly:
Histotoxic anoxia is a failure at the cellular level. Oxygen is in the environment, the airway is patent, the lungs and blood are normal and delivery is intact, but the cells cannot use the oxygen.

Contrasts with the other types:
- Anoxic: not enough oxygen reaches the blood.
- Anaemic: the blood cannot carry oxygen, as in CO poisoning.
- Stagnant: delivery fails, as in shock or heart failure.

Other points the guide gives about cyanide:
- It is listed among chemical asphyxiants, alongside carbon monoxide and hydrogen sulfide, where inhalation prevents utilisation of oxygen at the cellular level.
- Lividity is cherry pink.
- Rigor mortis develops early.
- It is not a cause of apparent death, because it causes rapid true death.

questions.text: Vagus nerve shares the same root with:
questions.explanation: CN IX and CN X arise together from the medulla and leave the skull through the jugular foramen.
questions.eshrahly:
This anatomy underlies reflex cardiac arrest in neck compression. Pressure on the carotid sinus sends afferent impulses along the glossopharyngeal nerve (CN IX). The efferent limb is the vagus (CN X), which inhibits the heart. Vagal cardiac inhibition can therefore cause death without prolonged anoxia.
ConditionReflex/vagal contribution to death
HangingVagal cardiac inhibition
Ligature strangulationReflex cardiac inhibition
ThrottlingReflex cardiac inhibition
ChokingReflex cardiac inhibition (a foreign body in the larynx can trigger vagal bronchospasm and stop the heart)
DrowningIndirect cause: reflex cardiac inhibition from vagal stimulation

allQuestions.text: Burking is:
allQuestions.explanation: Burking combines compression of the chest (traumatic asphyxia) with closure of the nose and mouth (smothering). This is the Burke and Hare method.
allQuestions.eshrahly:
Burking is a homicidal method that joins two mechanisms. The killer kneels or sits on the victim's chest while closing the nose and mouth with a hand (Burke and Hare, Edinburgh 1828). It may leave few external signs. Smothering by itself rarely produces petechiae, significant cyanosis or congestion unless the victim struggles. Traumatic asphyxia, in contrast, produces dramatic congestion and petechiae.
MechanismWhat happensTypical manner
Traumatic asphyxiaA heavy weight presses on the chest or upper abdomen and makes respiration impossible. Findings: congestion, cyanosis, petechiae, a line of demarcation.Mostly accidental, may be homicidal
SmotheringThe external respiratory openings are occluded by a hand or soft objects.Homicidal or accidental
BurkingTraumatic asphyxia and smothering together.Homicidal

allQuestions.text: The most common cause of inward (central) hyoid bone fracture is:
allQuestions.explanation: Throttling (manual strangulation) is the most common cause of hyoid bone fracture, and the fracture is inward.
allQuestions.eshrahly:
Throttling is constriction of the neck by the hand. The direct, forceful and repeated finger pressure damages the deep neck structures. Its findings are multiple contusions and fingernail abrasions on the neck, inward fracture of the hyoid and of the thyroid cartilage, and contusions of the deep tissues of the neck. Throttling is homicidal by definition, because grip relaxes as consciousness is lost.
Form of neck compressionInternal neck findings
ThrottlingInward hyoid fracture (the most common cause of hyoid fracture), thyroid cartilage fracture, deep muscle bruising
Ligature strangulationInward hyoid fracture, possible thyroid cartilage fracture, contusions and lacerations of neck muscles
Ordinary (suicidal) hangingUsually little internal damage
Judicial long-drop hangingExtensive neck laceration, torn sternomastoids, fracture-dislocation of C2–C3

allQuestions.text: Which method of asphyxia shows MOST severe internal neck damage:
allQuestions.explanation: Throttling involves direct, forceful, repeated finger pressure, which causes extensive deep-muscle bruising and fractures of the hyoid and thyroid cartilage. Ordinary hanging usually causes little internal damage.
allQuestions.eshrahly:
The amount of internal damage follows how the force is applied. In throttling the hand grips the neck directly. This explains the deep contusions and the cartilage and hyoid fractures. In ordinary hanging the body's own weight acts through a ligature, and internal damage is usually minimal. Massive damage in a hanging suggests a judicial long drop. The cause of death also differs between the forms.

Throttling causes death by:
- mechanical anoxia
- reflex cardiac inhibition
- cerebral anoxia
- delayed glottic oedema and choking

Hanging causes death mainly by cerebral ischaemia from carotid compression, with vagal cardiac inhibition and mechanical anoxia also contributing. Severe internal neck injury should therefore point first to throttling, or to a judicial hanging.

allQuestions.text: Which one causes severe damage to internal neck structures:
allQuestions.explanation: Throttling produces extensive deep-muscle bruising and fractures of the hyoid and thyroid cartilage. Ordinary hanging, complete or incomplete, usually causes little internal damage.
allQuestions.eshrahly:
Complete and incomplete hanging are both suspension of the body from the neck by a ligature. They differ in how much of the body weight is carried by the ligature, not in the amount of internal injury.
FeatureComplete hangingIncomplete hanging
Body weightFully suspended, feet off the groundPartly suspended, feet or knees may touch the ground
Main cause of deathCerebral ischaemiaAsphyxia
FaceLess congested, sometimes paleMarkedly congested
Internal neck damageUsually little in ordinary hanging. Massive damage means judicial long-drop hanging.
Throttling is the form in which deep neck tissues and cartilages are directly crushed by fingers.

allQuestions.text: The findings on the neck: extensive laceration, tears in sternomastoid and fracture-dislocation of C2-C3 vertebrae. These findings are present in:
allQuestions.explanation: Extensive neck lacerations, torn sternomastoids and C2–C3 fracture-dislocation (hangman's fracture) with cord transection are the picture of judicial (long-drop) hanging. Ordinary hanging usually causes little internal damage.
allQuestions.eshrahly:
Judicial (long-drop) hanging is the form in which the cause of death is transection of the spinal cord, and death is instant. The characteristic findings are extensive neck lacerations, torn sternomastoid muscles, and fracture-dislocation of C2–C3, the "hangman's fracture" of C2 (a bilateral pars-articularis fracture). This differs from the other forms of hanging. In suicidal, accidental, incomplete and autoerotic hanging, the neck usually shows only a ligature mark, and death is mainly from cerebral ischaemia, vagal inhibition or mechanical anoxia.

Autoerotic (sexual) asphyxia is usually by hanging, with anoxia induced deliberately to heighten arousal. It can resemble a suicidal hanging, but it does not produce this destructive neck injury.

allQuestions.text: Ligature mark of strangulation characteristics:
allQuestions.explanation: A ligature strangulation mark is transverse (horizontal), low (below the thyroid cartilage) and complete (encircles the whole neck). Hanging is the opposite: oblique, high and incomplete.
allQuestions.eshrahly:
In strangulation, the constricting force comes from the ligature itself, and it is applied evenly around the neck. In hanging, the body weight pulls the ligature upward toward the suspension point.
Feature of the ligature markHanging (incomplete)Ligature strangulation
LevelHigh, above the thyroid cartilageLow, below the thyroid cartilage
DirectionObliqueTransverse
ContinuityIncomplete (does not encircle the neck)Complete (encircles the neck)
DepthDeep, fading gradually toward the suspension pointDeep all through
The mark may show the shape of the ligating material, as a crush abrasion with a parchment-like quality. It is less visible with thick hair, a high collar, or a broad, soft ligature. It is more visible with a thin, rough, wire or metal ligature and with a longer duration of constriction.

allQuestions.text: Strangulation with ligature:
options: Associated with multiple lines on the neck
Marks are high in the neck
originalOptions: Associated with multiple lines on the neck
Marks are high in the neck
allQuestions.explanation: Ligature strangulation produces transverse, complete marks low in the neck. This is the reverse of hanging, whose marks are high, oblique and incomplete.
allQuestions.eshrahly:
Ligature strangulation is mechanical anoxic death caused by constriction of the neck by a ligature that occludes the air passages from outside. The constricting force is not the body's own suspended weight, which is the difference from hanging.

Causes of death:
- mechanical anoxia
- reflex cardiac inhibition
- delayed oedema of the glottis and choking, which can kill even some time after the ligature has been removed

Other findings:
- abrasions and contusions taking the shape of the ligating material
- inward fracture of the hyoid, possibly of the thyroid cartilage
- contusions and lacerations of neck muscles

The manner is homicidal or accidental, but not suicidal. A person cannot maintain ligature pressure on their own neck after losing consciousness. Any ligature mark on the neck is presumed to be homicide (strangulation) until proven otherwise.

allQuestions.text: Abrasions found on the neck are always considered what until proved otherwise?
allQuestions.explanation: Neck marks are presumed to be strangulation (homicide) until proven otherwise. This is the reverse default of hanging, which is more often self-inflicted.
allQuestions.eshrahly:
Location matters in interpreting abrasions. An abrasion pattern on the neck raises suspicion for throttling (manual strangulation). Fingernails leave small crescent-shaped (semilunar) abrasions when pressed in, or linear scratches when dragged. These are classic on the neck in throttling. A ligature mark on the neck is a crush (pressure) abrasion that reproduces the shape of the ligating material, and it is presumed homicidal until proven otherwise.

Both throttling and ligature strangulation are, by definition or by default, homicidal. Throttling is always homicidal. Ligature strangulation is homicidal or accidental, never suicidal. Hanging, by contrast, can be suicidal, homicidal or accidental, and the manner is never assumed from the mechanism alone.

allQuestions.text: True about the frothy secretions in drowning:
allQuestions.explanation: Drowning froth is white (may be pink-tinged), fine, lathery, tenacious and persistent. Coarse, offensive froth is putrefactive, not drowning froth.
allQuestions.eshrahly:
Froth at the mouth and nostrils is a sure external sign of drowning and an ante-mortem sign. It forms from air, water and mucus whipped together by continued respiratory effort. It will not form if the body was already dead and was dumped in the water afterward.
FeatureDrowning frothPutrefactive froth
ColourWhite (may be pink-tinged)Red-brown
TextureFine, latheryCoarse
PersistenceTenacious and persistent, re-forms after wipingNot described as persistent
SmellNot describedOffensive

allQuestions.text: Froth after drowning is:
allQuestions.explanation: Drowning froth is white (may be pink-tinged), fine and lathery, formed from air, water and mucus. Bloody or coarse froth does not describe it.
allQuestions.eshrahly:
The signs of drowning separate into sure and probable ones.
CategorySignMeaning
Sure externalFroth at the mouth and/or nostrilsAnte-mortem sign: the victim was alive and breathing when entering the water
Sure externalCadaveric spasmAnte-mortem sign: proof of life at entry into water (e.g. clutched weeds)
ProbableCyanosisRelated to anoxic anoxia
ProbablePale, wet skin; goose skin; washerwoman's skinRelated to the body being in water
ProbablePost-mortem injuries (animal bites, water movement, sand or rocks)Occur after death in water
The key investigative question is whether the person was alive when they went into the water or already dead. Froth and cadaveric spasm answer it.

allQuestions.text: The dead body is lying on autopsy table. There is leathery, fine, tenacious, persistent froth at mouth and nostrils. The death is due to:
allQuestions.explanation: Fine, tenacious, persistent froth at the mouth and nostrils is the sure external sign of drowning. It is formed by respiratory effort during submersion.
allQuestions.eshrahly:
Drowning is mechanical anoxic death due to submersion of the respiratory openings under water.

Causes of death:
- direct cause: mechanical anoxia
- indirect causes: reflex cardiac inhibition from vagal stimulation, and head injury or other fatal injuries sustained before or during submersion

The manner may be homicidal, suicidal or accidental. Water immersion alters the usual timeline of post-mortem changes, so cooling, hypostasis, adipocere and putrefaction are all affected. This matters when estimating time of death.

allQuestions.text: In drowning, the finding most indicative of TIME PASSED since death:
allQuestions.explanation: Washerwoman's skin shows how long the body has been in water (time since immersion), not the cause of death. Froth indicates life at entry into the water.
allQuestions.eshrahly:
Maceration of the hands and feet begins within hours and progresses to peeling ("glove and stocking" skin) over days to weeks, faster in warm water. A body dumped after death macerates too, so it cannot show that the person drowned.
SignWhat it tells you
Froth at mouth/nostrilsAlive and breathing at submersion (ante-mortem)
Cadaveric spasmAlive at entry into the water (ante-mortem)
Washerwoman's skinDuration of immersion
Goose skin (cutis anserina)Probable sign related to the body being in water
Note that the guide words this sign as time since immersion.

allQuestions.text: In drowning – one is indicated for time passed since death:
allQuestions.explanation: Maceration progresses with time in water, so it indicates how long the body has been immersed. Froth is an ante-mortem sign of drowning, not a measure of time.
allQuestions.eshrahly:
Being in water changes the normal timeline of post-mortem changes. Cooling, hypostasis, adipocere and putrefaction are all altered by immersion.

- Decomposition in water is slow, because of exclusion of air, protection by clothes and early cooling.
- Hypostasis in drowning is often faint, because moving water keeps turning the body. A floating body usually lies face-down with the head dependent, so lividity appears in the face, upper chest and upper limbs.
- Washerwoman's skin is a time-in-water marker. Goose skin is a probable sign related to the body being in water.

For these reasons, time-of-death estimates in drowning cases have to be made cautiously.

allQuestions.text: Traumatic asphyxia shows:
allQuestions.explanation: Chest compression blocks venous return from the head. This causes intense congestion and petechiae above the level of compression, ending at a sharp line of demarcation.
allQuestions.eshrahly:
Traumatic asphyxia occurs when a heavy weight presses on the chest or upper abdomen and makes respiration impossible. It is typically seen in "riot-crush", when a crowd compresses the chest.
AspectDetails
Causes of deathMechanical anoxia, injury to vital organs, positional asphyxia where mechanisms overlap
FindingsContusions and abrasions of the chest and abdomen, fractured ribs, rupture of internal organs
Skin pictureIntense congestion, cyanosis and huge numbers of petechiae over face, neck and upper chest; line of demarcation between the discoloured upper body and the normal lower part
MannerMostly accidental, may be homicidal
Cherry-red colour belongs to carbon monoxide poisoning, and adipocere is a late post-mortem change.

allQuestions.text: Clear line of demarcation on the neck is always seen in:
allQuestions.explanation: Traumatic asphyxia produces a sharp line of demarcation at the level of chest compression, between the discoloured upper body and the normal lower part.
allQuestions.eshrahly:
The line of demarcation is the signature of traumatic asphyxia. It marks the level of compression. Above it the face, neck and upper chest show intense congestion, cyanosis and numerous petechiae (an "ecchymotic mask"). Below it the body looks normal.

The cause is blocked venous return from the head. Hanging, gagging and drowning do not produce this pattern. Gagging means a cloth is pushed into or across the mouth, with progressive asphyxia as the nares close from mucus and oedema.

In the guide the line is at the level of compression, which is usually the chest or upper abdomen, rather than literally on the neck.

allQuestions.text: Petechial hemorrhages are typically seen in which condition?
allQuestions.explanation: Massive petechiae over the face, neck and upper chest point to traumatic (crush or riot) asphyxia.
allQuestions.eshrahly:
Petechiae are pinpoint haemorrhages from rupture of small vessels, predominantly small venules. The rupture appears to be mechanical, caused by sudden over-distension after an abrupt rise in intravascular pressure. They are found above the level of the obstruction. The most common sites are the visceral pleura and the epicardium. They also appear in the conjunctivae and sclerae, where venules are unsupported by surrounding tissue.
Classical signWhat it is
CongestionRed face and head from venous filling when venous return is obstructed
OedemaTransudation of fluid from veins under raised venous pressure
CyanosisIncrease in reduced haemoglobin, observable from about 5 g/100 mL
PetechiaeRuptured venules in skin, eyes, pleura and epicardium
Petechiae are non-specific. They also occur in MI, asthma and whooping cough, so alone they do not prove asphyxia.

allQuestions.text: Cause of death in mechanical asphyxia includes all of the following EXCEPT:
allQuestions.explanation: Mechanical asphyxia kills by anoxia, pulmonary oedema, reflex vagal cardiac inhibition and cerebral ischaemia. Sepsis is not one of these mechanisms.
allQuestions.eshrahly:
The underlying mechanism of death in mechanical (violent) asphyxia is usually a combination of neck compression, airway blockage, compression of the chest or face, and chemical asphyxia or lack of oxygen. Delayed glottic oedema can also kill after the ligature is removed. Reflex cardiac arrest works through a defined pathway. Pressure on the carotid sinus sends afferent impulses along the glossopharyngeal nerve (CN IX), and the efferent limb is the vagus (CN X).
TypeCauses of death
HangingCerebral ischaemia (commonest), vagal cardiac inhibition, mechanical anoxia; cord transection in judicial hanging
Ligature strangulationMechanical anoxia, reflex cardiac inhibition, delayed glottic oedema
ThrottlingMechanical anoxia, reflex cardiac inhibition, cerebral anoxia, delayed glottic oedema
ChokingReflex cardiac inhibition, mechanical anoxia
DrowningMechanical anoxia; indirect: vagal cardiac inhibition, associated head injury

allQuestions.text: Mechanical asphyxia is type of:
allQuestions.explanation: In mechanical (violent) asphyxia, an external force obstructing the airway prevents enough oxygen reaching the blood. This is anoxic anoxia.
allQuestions.eshrahly:
Hypoxia means low oxygen and anoxia means without oxygen. Each type of anoxia corresponds to a failure at a different point in the oxygen chain.
TypeProblemExamples
AnoxicNot enough oxygen reaches the bloodHigh altitude, respiratory centre depression (morphine), paralysis (anaesthetics, Guillain–Barré), mechanical asphyxia, pulmonary embolism
AnaemicBlood cannot carry oxygen properlySevere anaemia, CO (carboxyhaemoglobin), haemolysis, haemorrhage
StagnantCirculation or delivery to tissue failsShock, heart failure, local vascular obstruction
HistotoxicTissues cannot use delivered oxygenCyanide (cytochrome oxidase inhibition)
Once the airway is obstructed, three stages follow: forced respiration, convulsions, and paralysis. Death occurs in about 5 minutes overall.

allQuestions.text: The cause of death in an environment with DECREASED O2 levels will be:
allQuestions.explanation: Low ambient oxygen (e.g. high altitude) means too little oxygen enters the blood, which is anoxic anoxia. This is the ambient subtype.
allQuestions.eshrahly:
Anoxic anoxia has several subtypes. Mechanical is only one of them, so the option "mechanical anoxia" does not describe a low-oxygen atmosphere.
Subtype of anoxic anoxiaMechanismExample
AmbientLow ambient oxygenHigh altitude
CentralDepression of the respiratory centreMorphine overdose, medullary herniation
ParalyticPeripheral nerve injury or drug paralysisAnaesthetic drugs, Guillain–Barré
Mechanical (violent asphyxia)External force obstructing the airwaySmothering, gagging, choking, strangulation
Pulmonary blood flow obstructionNo perfusion of the lungPulmonary embolism
Normal oxygenation requires an oxygen-containing environment, a patent airway, normal lungs, blood supply to the lungs, a working respiratory centre, a normal chest wall, a functioning heart and blood able to carry oxygen.

allQuestions.text: NOT of the TRIAD features of asphyxia:
options: Fluid in the left side of the heart
Petechial hemorrhages in skin of face and eyes
originalOptions: Fluid in the left side of the heart
Petechial hemorrhages in skin of face and eyes
allQuestions.correctAnswer: B) Fluid in the left side of the heart
allQuestions.correctAnswerText: Fluid in the left side of the heart
allQuestions.explanation: The exam triad is congestion, cyanosis and petechial haemorrhages. Fluid in the left side of the heart is not a feature of asphyxia.
allQuestions.eshrahly:
The classical features of asphyxia are found where air passages are obstructed by pressure on the neck or chest: congestion, oedema, cyanosis and petechial haemorrhages. Exam questions often use the triad of congestion, cyanosis and petechiae. Older texts describe a distended right heart and engorged great veins, not fluid in the left heart.

Points to remember:
- Increased fluidity of the blood was taught as a fifth classical feature but is now rejected, a classic exam trap.
- The signs are very non-specific and unreliable. Even several together do not prove mechanical asphyxia.
- If death occurs very rapidly, the signs may not have time to develop.
- The slower the death, the more prominent the signs.
- The correct approach combines history and circumstances, exclusion of other causes and cautious evaluation of the signs.

allQuestions.text: How are antemortem hangings diagnosed?
options: By the presence of cadaveric spasm
By vital reaction signs (hemorrhage in ligature mark, skin abrasion)
originalOptions: By the presence of cadaveric spasm
By vital reaction signs (hemorrhage in ligature mark, skin abrasion)
allQuestions.correctAnswer: B) By vital reaction signs (hemorrhage in ligature mark, skin abrasion)
allQuestions.correctAnswerText: By vital reaction signs (hemorrhage in ligature mark, skin abrasion)
allQuestions.explanation: Ante-mortem hanging is proved by vital reaction in the ligature mark: bruising or haemorrhage in the base and margins of the groove, reddened edges, and inflammatory cells on histology.
allQuestions.eshrahly:
A body hanged after death shows a pale, parchment-like groove with no vital reaction. In ante-mortem hanging the ligature mark shows bruising and haemorrhage in the base and margins, with reddened edges and inflammatory cells on histology. Supporting findings are dribbling of saliva, congestion and petechiae above the mark, and carotid intimal tears.

Caution on timing: white blood cells remain capable of movement for up to 12 hours after cardiac arrest. This makes microscopic identification of a vital reaction of doubtful reliability when judging ante- versus post-mortem timing.

Cadaveric spasm and livor patterns are not the diagnostic test for ante-mortem hanging.

allQuestions.text: Sign of antemortem hanging:
allQuestions.explanation: Dribbling of saliva is the most important sign for hanging and is an ante-mortem sign.
allQuestions.eshrahly:
The post-mortem picture of hanging has general and special features.
FeatureFinding in hanging
TongueProtrusion
SalivaDribbling: the most important sign, ante-mortem
HypostasisLower half of the body
NeckElongated, with the head tilted to the opposite side from the suspension point
Ligature markHigh, oblique and incomplete, with an imprint of the ligature material
Asphyxial signs are non-specific: congestion alone or petechiae alone do not prove hanging.

allQuestions.text: Dripping of saliva occurs in:
allQuestions.explanation: Dribbling of saliva is an ante-mortem sign of hanging, so it is not seen in a body hanged after death.
allQuestions.eshrahly:
Saliva dribbling is the most important sign for hanging. It is an ante-mortem finding, which makes it useful in separating a true hanging from a body strung up after death. It differs between the two forms of hanging.
PointComplete hangingIncomplete hanging
Dribbling of salivaPositiveNegative
Tear in carotid intimaPositiveNegative
FaceLess congested, sometimes paleMarkedly congested
Manner may be suicidal, homicidal or accidental.

allQuestions.text: Hypostasis in lower limbs is a sign of:
allQuestions.explanation: In complete hanging the body is fully suspended, so blood pools in the dependent lower half. In incomplete hanging the hypostasis follows whichever part touches the ground.
allQuestions.eshrahly:
After death, blood moves only under gravity, so lividity shows the posture of the body. Lividity starts immediately, is apparent after about 2 hours, and begins to fix around 6–8 hours. Before fixation it can shift if the body is moved. A body moved after death may show two overlapping patterns (dual lividity).
Body positionDistribution of lividity
Vertical (hanging)Distal: legs, feet, hands
Incomplete hangingAccording to the part touching the ground
Drowning (floating face-down)Chest, upper chest, upper limbs

allQuestions.text: Abrasions around the mouth indicate:
allQuestions.explanation: Smothering involves a hand or soft object over the nose and mouth. Fingernail abrasions around the nose and mouth are classic.
allQuestions.eshrahly:
Smothering is mechanical anoxic death caused by occlusion of the external respiratory openings by the hand or soft objects. Findings are multiple contusions and fingernail abrasions, contusions in the buccal mucosa, and ventral hypostasis in cot death. If the victim struggles, there may be bruises and abrasions on the face and lips and inside the mouth, where the lips are pressed against the teeth.

Smothering may leave almost no signs.
- Pressure over the nose and mouth only very rarely causes petechiae, significant cyanosis or congestion unless the victim struggles.
- It may be virtually impossible to diagnose in the old, the infirm or the very young. This matters for elder abuse and infant deaths that may be mistaken for natural or SIDS deaths.
- Plastic bag suffocation typically shows no classic asphyxial signs, and the face is usually pale. The "Exit" method is an example.

Manner is homicidal or accidental.

allQuestions.text: Manner of death in choking:
allQuestions.explanation: Choking is mainly accidental, classically a small child choking on a button or small object. Homicidal choking is possible in principle but rare.
allQuestions.eshrahly:
Choking is mechanical anoxic death from occlusion of the respiratory passages from inside, at the larynx, classically by a foreign body. It can cause sudden cardiac death through vagal reflex pathways, not only by blocking airflow. Causes of death are reflex cardiac inhibition and mechanical anoxia.
TypeSite/mechanism of obstructionManner
SmotheringExternal openings (nose, mouth) occluded by hand or soft objectHomicidal or accidental
GaggingCloth pushed into or across the mouth; breathing continues via the nose at firstOften seen in robbery
ChokingRespiratory passages occluded from inside, at the larynxMainly accidental

allQuestions.text: Histotoxic anoxia is caused by:
allQuestions.explanation: Cyanide inhibits cytochrome oxidase, so tissues cannot use oxygen even though delivery is normal. This is histotoxic anoxia.
allQuestions.eshrahly:
In histotoxic anoxia, oxygen is delivered normally but the cells cannot use it. The classic cause is cyanide, which inhibits cytochrome oxidase. The same mitochondrial enzyme is affected by carbon monoxide, discussed in the toxicology section.

How the other options relate:
- CO is classed as anaemic anoxia in the guide: it forms carboxyhaemoglobin, which reduces the blood's ability to carry oxygen.
- Morphine causes anoxic anoxia of the central type, by depressing the respiratory centre.

Lividity colour is cherry pink in CO poisoning, in cold, and in cyanide poisoning.

allQuestions.text: Complete hanging is related to:
allQuestions.explanation: Complete hanging means the full body weight is suspended with the feet off the ground. Incomplete hanging is partial suspension.
allQuestions.eshrahly:
A common misconception is that hanging requires the full body weight to be suspended in the air. Incomplete hanging, with feet or knees still touching the ground, can still be fatal. A hanging survivor should be kept under observation even if apparently well, because laryngeal oedema from neck compression may compromise the airway later.
PointComplete hangingIncomplete hanging
Other nameHigh point hangingLow point hanging
Touching the groundNegativePositive
Main cause of deathCerebral ischaemiaAsphyxia
HypostasisLower half of the bodyAccording to the part touching the ground
KnotFixed knot or running nooseAlways a running noose
Ligature markIncomplete, above the thyroid cartilage, oblique, deep, fading toward the suspension pointComplete, below the thyroid cartilage, transverse, deep all through

allQuestions.text: Death of 65-year-old person dropped in sea water. Skin showing goose skin appearance, hair easily removed. Right hand grasping forcefully grass weeds. This is consistent with:
allQuestions.explanation: Forceful grasping of weeds or grass in a drowning victim is cadaveric spasm. It proves the person was alive at the time of entry into the water.
allQuestions.eshrahly:
Cadaveric spasm (instantaneous rigor) occurs at the moment of death and may persist into the period of rigor mortis. Its cause is unknown, but it is usually associated with violent deaths with intense emotion. It affects only selected muscles that were contracted at death, and it often demonstrates the last activity before death, for example gripping a knife.
PointRigor mortisCadaveric spasm
OnsetDelayed, 2–3 hoursInstantaneous
DurationUp to 36 hoursA few hours, until replaced by rigor
IntensityComparatively moderateComparatively very strong
MechanismATP falls below a critical levelUnknown
MusclesAll muscles, graduallyOnly muscles contracted at death
Goose skin is a probable drowning sign. Cadaveric spasm is one of the sure ante-mortem drowning signs.

allQuestions.text: Guillain-Barré syndrome (GBS) causes what type of anoxia:
options: Anoxic anoxia (hypoxic hypoxia) – respiratory muscle paralysis prevents air entry
originalOptions: Anoxic anoxia (hypoxic hypoxia) – respiratory muscle paralysis prevents air entry
allQuestions.correctAnswer: A) Anoxic anoxia (hypoxic hypoxia) – respiratory muscle paralysis prevents air entry
allQuestions.correctAnswerText: Anoxic anoxia (hypoxic hypoxia) – respiratory muscle paralysis prevents air entry
allQuestions.explanation: Guillain–Barré causes paralytic anoxic anoxia. Peripheral nerve injury stops respiration, so not enough oxygen reaches the blood.
allQuestions.eshrahly:
Anoxic anoxia means oxygen does not reach the blood in adequate amounts. The paralytic subtype covers anaesthetic drugs and Guillain–Barré syndrome with peripheral nerve injury. It should be distinguished from the central subtype (respiratory centre depression, e.g. morphine overdose or medullary herniation).
Site of failureExample
Respiratory centreMorphine overdose, medullary herniation
Peripheral nerves / musclesGuillain–Barré, anaesthetic drugs
AirwayMechanical asphyxia
Pulmonary blood flowPulmonary embolism

allQuestions.text: What type of asphyxia is caused by cyanide (HCN)?
allQuestions.explanation: Cyanide inhibits cytochrome oxidase. Oxygen is delivered normally, but the tissues cannot retrieve it.
allQuestions.eshrahly:
Histotoxic anoxia is a failure at the cellular level. Oxygen is in the environment, the airway is patent, the lungs and blood are normal and delivery is intact, but the cells cannot use the oxygen.

Contrasts with the other types:
- Anoxic: not enough oxygen reaches the blood.
- Anaemic: the blood cannot carry oxygen, as in CO poisoning.
- Stagnant: delivery fails, as in shock or heart failure.

Other points the guide gives about cyanide:
- It is listed among chemical asphyxiants, alongside carbon monoxide and hydrogen sulfide, where inhalation prevents utilisation of oxygen at the cellular level.
- Lividity is cherry pink.
- Rigor mortis develops early.
- It is not a cause of apparent death, because it causes rapid true death.

allQuestions.text: Vagus nerve shares the same root with:
allQuestions.explanation: CN IX and CN X arise together from the medulla and leave the skull through the jugular foramen.
allQuestions.eshrahly:
This anatomy underlies reflex cardiac arrest in neck compression. Pressure on the carotid sinus sends afferent impulses along the glossopharyngeal nerve (CN IX). The efferent limb is the vagus (CN X), which inhibits the heart. Vagal cardiac inhibition can therefore cause death without prolonged anoxia.
ConditionReflex/vagal contribution to death
HangingVagal cardiac inhibition
Ligature strangulationReflex cardiac inhibition
ThrottlingReflex cardiac inhibition
ChokingReflex cardiac inhibition (a foreign body in the larynx can trigger vagal bronchospasm and stop the heart)
DrowningIndirect cause: reflex cardiac inhibition from vagal stimulation
